what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: Two commits, two substantive, and both of them real: the value arm is now at HEAD and the zero-carbon must-run fleet is read half-hourly instead of assumed flat. So the previous direction steered and the machine took it. But the finding of this stretch is that four consecutive records -- mine included -- have misdiagnosed why publishing keeps dying, and the machine's own log has been holding the answer the whole time. Publishing has been down since 00:21 UTC. `docs/observability/.publish_gate_state.json` reads `total_red: 0`, `blocking_tests: []`, `suspects: {}`, and records the kind as `commit_did_not_land` with the prose "refused/timed out/never reached origin". `docs/observability/sim-runner-log.md:203191` records the same event as `[test-gate] TESTS FAILED -- COMMIT REFUSED`, `6 failed, 471 passed in 636.44s`, with all six nodes named. The gate did not time out; it finished in 636s inside a budget of 840s that was raised yesterday to fix a problem that was not this one. And the six reds have one cause: `tests/tools/test_generate_proof_coupled_gaps.py::test_empty_ledger_fails_ closed_not_silent` fails on `expected_ge_l2` being empty -- "fail-open guard: expected >=1 coupled world atom at >=L2 in the live map", `assert set()`. There are no coupled world atoms at L2 in the live map because the live map is the 74-atom half of a split that has never landed. I reproduced this: HEAD plus the two staged map halves and nothing else reds five level-sensitive tests with "store holds records but no such atom in the map" for A1, A2, A9, W4_2, W4_3, W4_4, W5_1 and the rest of the 224. So the publish wedge IS the half-rolled map split, and the publisher has been trying to commit that 224-atom truncation every forty minutes since midnight with the gate correctly refusing it each time. The gate is the only thing standing between this project and a record that has lost three quarters of its atoms. Against the thesis proper the position is better than last night and still not claimable. The value arm is genuinely per-customer at HEAD -- 263 accounts, 187 distinct margins, the modal margin covering 1.9% of the book, verified from the committed blob. What sits one commit behind it is more important than the arm: `tools/couple_value_based_pricing.py` now writes a `shared_calibration` block that states the company's churn estimator and the world's `churn_position_multiplier` both descend from the same DESNZ 2015-2025 series, sets `publishable_as_evidence_of_inference: false`, flags that 193 of 263 accounts (73.4%) were scored beyond the world's own calibration, and says what would discharge it. That is the company declining to claim an advantage it cannot separate from shared arithmetic, and it is the most thesis-honest artefact this project has produced. It is uncommitted, and it is uncommitted because of the same map split. On the previous focus: item one was named and NOT drawn, for a reason worth recording -- the worker that landed the value arm looked at the split, correctly identified sweeping it as the hazard CLAUDE.md names, and left it "for the lane that owns the split". No lane owns it. The discipline that stops one lane eating another's work has no counterpart that assigns a large in-flight write to somebody, so it has sat for three records getting more dangerous. That is the drift, and it is structural, not laziness.

focus.what: Land the map split as ONE commit, then its re-filer as the immediately next commit, with nothing landing in between. The pathspec is the IMPORT CLOSURE, not the seven paths my last record named -- derive it with `grep -rl maturity_map_store --include=*.py background/ tools/ site/ tests/`, which returns 52 files (50 modified, 2 untracked), and add `docs/design/maturity_map.yaml`, `docs/design/maturity_map_closed.yaml`, `docs/design/MAP_SPLIT_2026-08-26.md`, `docs/design/MATURITY_MAP.md` and `tests/tools/test_couple_value_based_pricing.py` (that last one because `tools/couple_value_based_pricing.py` is inside the closure and must not land without its own control). Before landing, assert on HEAD+pathspec -- not the worktree -- that `tests/tools/test_generate_proof_coupled_gaps.py`, `tests/background/test_derived_artefact_register.py`, `tests/design/test_atom_records_store.py`, `tests/design/test_maturity_map_facets.py` and `tests/test_coupled_triad_gate.py` are all green; the two `TestStaleness` nodes may have a second cause, so if they stay red after the split lands, diagnose them separately rather than holding the split. Then add `maturity_map_store.refile()` -- move any atom whose half disagrees with `is_closed` into the correct half as one two-file write, BOTH directions -- call it from `merge_atom_status.merge()` after the field fold, make the fold stage `MAP_PARTS_REL` rather than `MAP_REL`, and mutation-test it both directions plus a null control per R15. Use `python3 -m tools.surgical_land`, never `--no-verify`, and do not wrap it in `timeout`.
focus.why: This one commit is the publish wedge, the record-destruction hazard and the tree-wide wedge, all three. Publishing is down because the gate keeps refusing a commit that would delete 224 atoms; the co-calibration record and the coupler are stranded behind it; 50 modules in the working tree import a file git has never seen, so the supervisor that reads the working tree is running today on a module that does not exist at HEAD. And the re-filer is not optional polish: `tests/tools/test_maturity_map_store.py::test_the_split_predicate_agrees_with_where_ every_atom_actually_SITS` reds the moment any atom's level reaches its own, that test sits on the tree-wide selection so it refuses EVERY lane, and `EP13_adapter_carbon_intensity` -- level 2 heading for 3, `loop_stage: build`, drawn right now -- is the atom that arms it. Landing the split without the re-filer trades one incident for a worse one. Done when HEAD holds all of it, `map_store.load_atoms()` reads 298 from HEAD, the named tests are green in the gated tree, the re-filer's mutation tests fire in both directions, and the next publish cycle records a success rather than a sixth `commit_did_not_land`.

focus.what: Make `.publish_gate_state.json` carry what the publisher already saw. In `background/process_run_complete.py`, the branch at ~4195 captures the hook chain's output into `_tail` and logs it, then calls `record_publish_gate_failure` with a prose `reason` and nothing else -- so the failing node IDs are written to `sim-runner-log.md` and discarded everywhere a reader would look. Pass the captured tail through, parse the `FAILED <nodeid>` lines out of it into `blocking_tests`, and populate `suspects` from their files. Mutation-test both ways per R15: a refusal carrying a known red must populate `blocking_tests`, and a clean empty-index no-op must leave it empty -- a parser that always finds something is the fail-open twin of the fail-silent it replaces.
focus.why: Tonight the state file said `total_red: 0`, `blocking_tests: []`, `suspects: {}` through five consecutive refusals whose log entries name six failing tests and print "COMMIT REFUSED". Yesterday's raise of `_COMMIT_DEADLINE` from 600 to 840 was bought with that blindness; tonight's gate finished in 636s and was refused on tests, so the deadline lever was never the lever. Fixing the split unwedges publishing once; this is what stops the next wedge costing a whole orientation to diagnose. The atom was drawn again this stretch and did not move, which is the signal: an estimator cannot be improved against a sample that excludes the accounts it is used on. what_next.why_this_is_here: Direction multiplies the draw's existing weights and can never zero one, so it can only ever be ignored -- never obeyed by force. Whether it was actually followed is therefore a measurement, not an assumption.

how_to_read_this: The delivery seat wakes on a timer, reads the last stretch, and writes direction -- never code. What it decides biases which work the ticks draw and can never block any of it. Everything on this page is read from a committed record; nothing here is computed a second time.
